infrastructure.name: Conventions & infrastructure
infrastructure.summary: Day counts, holiday calendars, business-day adjustment, spot lags and coupon schedules, in pure Python and tested against QuantLib. Every kit from the library includes it.
covers: TARGET, France, UK and US settlement calendars, joint calendars
Following, Modified Following, Preceding, Modified Preceding
Spot lags (T+2), month and year tenors with the end-of-month rule
infrastructure.tests: 611 tests against QuantLib reference values: 4,200 year fractions, every holiday 2000-2050, 500 adjustments, 400 date advances, 85 schedules. QuantLib is not needed to run them.
infrastructure.finding: QuantLib 1.44's French settlement calendar fixes Ascension on May 10 and Whit Monday on May 21; both move with Easter. The module uses the correct dates and documents the difference.

models.name: Black-Scholes
models.summary: Lognormal spot with constant volatility. The reference every equity and FX model is checked against, and the natural first Monte Carlo benchmark.
dynamics: dS = (r - q) S dt + σ S dW under the risk-neutral measure
C = S e^(-qT) N(d1) - K e^(-rT) N(d2), d1,2 = [ln(S/K) + (r - q ± σ²/2) T] / (σ√T)

parameters.name: σ
parameters.meaning: Volatility, constant across strikes and maturities

parameters.name: r, q
parameters.meaning: Continuously compounded rate and dividend (or foreign) yield

assumptions: Constant volatility: no smile, no term structure
limits: Use as benchmark and control variate, not as the production model for exotics
models.prototype: Closed-form pricer with Greeks, plus a Monte Carlo pricer (exact lognormal steps, antithetics, geometric-Asian control variate) that reports a standard error with every price.

tests.checks: C - P = S e^(-qT) - K e^(-rT)
Variance with and without the geometric-Asian control
tests.criterion: Variance reduction factor reported, above 10 at the money

tests.checks: Monte Carlo with the Broadie-Glasserman-Kou shift against the continuous closed form
tests.criterion: Within 3 standard errors plus 1% of price

tests.checks: Call price decreasing and convex in strike
σ → 0 gives discounted forward intrinsic; T → 0 gives intrinsic

tests.criterion: Spread consistent with the standard error

models.referenceContents: European prices and Greeks (54 cases, including a negative rate), discrete geometric Asian calls (18), continuously monitored barriers (24).

quantum.note: The textbook target for quantum amplitude estimation. A quantum pricer would have to beat this Monte Carlo after variance reduction, not plain Monte Carlo.

kit.summary: Prototype, 11 validation tests with pre-registered criteria (635 test cases with the conventions module), QuantLib reference values, test plan and pre-filled SR 11-7 documentation outline. Tested in a clean environment without QuantLib.

models.name: Heston
models.summary: Stochastic variance with mean reversion and spot-vol correlation. Produces a smile and a skew with five parameters, and has a semi-analytic price for Europeans.
dynamics: dS = (r - q) S dt + √v S dW₁
dv = κ(θ - v) dt + σ √v dW₂, d⟨W₁, W₂⟩ = ρ dt
European price by Fourier inversion of the characteristic function

parameters.name: ρ
parameters.meaning: Spot-variance correlation, negative for equity skew

limits: Short-maturity skew too flat without jumps
When the Feller condition 2κθ > σ² fails (common after calibration), naive Euler schemes are biased: use Andersen's QE scheme or full truncation
Characteristic-function integration needs care for short maturities and far strikes
models.prototype: Semi-analytic pricer (characteristic function in the stable 'little trap' form, numerical integration) and a Monte Carlo pricer with Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme.

tests.criterion: Within 3 standard errors at 50 steps per year

tests.checks: Price as the time step shrinks
tests.criterion: Bias reported and below 1 standard error at the chosen step
No negative or NaN prices; prices within no-arbitrage bounds

tests.checks: 2κθ - σ² reported for every parameter set
tests.criterion: Logged, with the scheme's behaviour documented when negative
Parameters and fitted prices stable within tolerance

models.referenceContents: European calls and puts for 3 parameter sets (one violating Feller), maturities 3 months to 5 years, strikes 70 to 140 (90 cases).

quantum.note: Path-dependent Monte Carlo under stochastic volatility is where amplitude estimation is studied, but loading the joint spot-variance distribution is the bottleneck. Fault-tolerant hardware required.

models.name: Hull-White one factor
models.summary: Gaussian short rate with mean reversion, fitted exactly to today's curve. Closed forms for bond options, caps and (via Jamshidian) swaptions.
dynamics: dr = [θ(t) - a r] dt + σ dW, θ(t) fitted to the initial discount curve

parameters.name: a
parameters.meaning: Mean reversion speed, drives the decorrelation of rates

assumptions: One factor: all rates perfectly correlated
limits: Cannot fit a full swaption cube; calibrate to the instruments that matter for the product
Single factor understates decorrelation for spread options and curve trades
models.prototype: Closed-form zero-coupon bond option and caplet pricer, and a short-rate Monte Carlo (exact Gaussian transition) that reprices the initial curve.

tests.checks: Calls and puts on zero-coupon bonds
Monte Carlo discount factors against the initial curve
tests.criterion: Within 3 standard errors for maturities to 30 years
Converges to the Ho-Lee closed form

tests.checks: Simulated option price against closed form
Pricing with a negative initial curve
a and σ refitted on perturbed co-terminal swaptions

models.referenceContents: Zero-coupon bond options for 3 parameter sets including a negative rate (72 cases), caps of 3 and 5 years (18).

quantum.note: Exposure simulation for XVA is a candidate for amplitude estimation, after regression-based exposures and AAD have been exhausted classically.

models.name: SABR
models.summary: Stochastic-volatility smile model for rates, with Hagan's expansion and its arbitrage-free variants.

models.name: Hazard-rate curve and CDS (ISDA standard model)
models.summary: Default intensity bootstrapped from CDS quotes, priced with the ISDA standard model.

models.name: Bates (Heston with jumps)
models.summary: Adds lognormal jumps to Heston for short-dated skew.

models.name: Heston stochastic local volatility
models.summary: Leverage function on top of Heston, fitted to the vanilla surface.

models.name: Merton jump diffusion
models.summary: Black-Scholes with lognormal jumps; series closed form.

models.name: CEV
models.summary: Local volatility as a power of spot.

models.name: G2++
models.summary: Two-factor Gaussian short rate for decorrelation.

models.name: Vasicek, CIR, Black-Karasinski
models.summary: Classic short-rate models, for teaching and specific uses.

models.summary: Joint lognormal or shifted dynamics of forward rates. QuantLib's Python bindings expose little of it.

models.name: One-factor Gaussian copula (Vasicek LHP)
